missions.profile: Wide-field infrared survey telescope with a Hubble-class mirror but a field of view roughly one hundred times larger, built to study dark energy and find exoplanets through microlensing and direct imaging.
NASA/ESA/CSA infrared flagship observing from Sun–Earth L2, covering everything from the first galaxies to exoplanet atmospheres.
The veteran NASA/ESA optical and ultraviolet observatory in low Earth orbit, still producing frontline science in its fourth decade.

NASA's programme to return astronauts to the Moon with commercial and international partners. Artemis II flew the first crewed mission in April 2026; under an accelerated plan, Artemis III will send four astronauts to low Earth orbit in 2027 to test critical systems ahead of a lunar landing targeted for 2028.
missions.status: Artemis III in preparation; landing targeted 2028

missions.profile: Europa Clipper is en route to assess the habitability of Jupiter's moon Europa, arriving in 2030; ESA's JUICE mission follows to the icy moons in 2031. NASA's Dragonfly mission to Saturn's moon Titan is planned for 2028.
Parker Solar Probe flies repeated record-close passes through the Sun's corona to trace how the solar wind is heated and accelerated.

NASA's surface fleet — the Perseverance and Curiosity rovers — continues exploring Jezero and Gale craters, with orbiters relaying data overhead. The twin ESCAPADE orbiters, which will study how the solar wind strips Mars's atmosphere, are en route after powered Earth flybys.
missions.status: Operating; ESCAPADE en route after Nov 2026 Earth flybys

missions.profile: Continuously crewed orbital laboratory operated with international partners, hosting rotating crews and microgravity research. Crew-13 took over in October 2026 after Crew-12 returned.
Joint ESA/JAXA mission carrying two orbiters to Mercury. After an eight-year cruise it is now in its arrival phase, ahead of orbit insertion.
ESA's Earth-watching fleet: the Copernicus Sentinels monitor land, ocean and atmosphere, now joined by Sentinel-3C and the FLEX Earth Explorer, which will map plant fluorescence globally.
missions.status: Operating; Sentinel-3C returned first images Oct 2026

missions.profile: Solar Orbiter studies the Sun at close range and from progressively tilted orbits, returning the first good views of the solar poles.
India's human spaceflight programme, working toward its first crewed orbital mission through uncrewed test flights and recovery testing.
missions.status: In development; CM–SM separation tests completed for uncrewed G1

missions.profile: Earth observation satellite providing imaging over the Indian region from geostationary orbit.
India's heaviest operational launch vehicle, used for Chandrayaan-3 and slated for Gaganyaan, powered by the CE20 cryogenic upper stage.
China's robotic lunar programme. Chang'e-6 returned the first far-side samples in 2024; Chang'e-7 and -8 target the lunar south pole ahead of a planned research station.
China's planetary exploration line: Tianwen-1 orbits Mars, Tianwen-2 is en route to sample the quasi-satellite Kamo'oalewa, and Tianwen-3 aims to return samples from Mars.
missions.expected: Tianwen-3 launch targeted 2028; Mars sample return around 2031

missions.profile: 8.4-metre survey telescope in Chile with the largest digital camera ever built, imaging the entire southern sky every few nights.
missions.expected: 10-year Legacy Survey of Space and Time

missions.profile: NASA's Earth-observing satellites, including the NASA/USGS Landsat series, track land, ice, ocean and atmosphere, with results published through NASA's Earth Observatory.
ESA's Jupiter Icy Moons Explorer (Juice) is cruising to Jupiter using a series of planetary gravity assists, to study Ganymede, Callisto and Europa from 2031.
missions.status: In transit; Earth flyby completed 28 Sep 2026

missions.profile: Mars Express, ESA's longest-serving Mars orbiter, images and maps the planet's surface, subsurface and atmosphere.
JAXA-led X-ray Imaging and Spectroscopy Mission, built with NASA, performing high-resolution X-ray spectroscopy of hot cosmic plasmas, from galaxy clusters to compact binary stars.
Compton Spectrometer and Imager, a NASA Small Explorer gamma-ray telescope being built at UC Berkeley to map how chemical elements form in the Milky Way.
NASA's flagship X-ray observatory, studying hot and energetic regions of the universe such as black holes, supernova remnants and galaxy clusters from a high elliptical Earth orbit.
China's modular space station in low Earth orbit, continuously crewed by rotating Shenzhou crews and preparing to host its first foreign astronaut from Pakistan.
Second-generation satellite for India's NavIC regional navigation system, part of the NVS series replacing the original IRNSS satellites.
Deep Atmosphere Venus Investigation of Noble gases, Chemistry, and Imaging: a NASA Venus mission whose descent probe will study the planet's deep atmosphere.
Solar wind Magnetosphere Ionosphere Link Explorer, a joint ESA–Chinese Academy of Sciences mission imaging how Earth's magnetosphere responds to the solar wind.
PRobe far-Infrared Mission for Astrophysics, a far-infrared observatory and the first mission in NASA’s new Probe Explorers class of astrophysics missions.
Thermal infraRed Imaging Satellite for High-resolution Natural resource Assessment, a joint ISRO–CNES mission to map land and water surface temperature for water-use and climate monitoring.
ESA's wide-field space telescope mapping the shapes and distribution of billions of galaxies across a third of the sky to probe dark matter and dark energy.
JAXA mission to Mars's moons Phobos and Deimos that will land on Phobos, collect a surface sample and return it to Earth — the first sample return from the Martian system.
missions.status: Launch scheduled 20 Oct 2026 (JST) on H3 F10
missions.expected: Sample return to Earth planned for 2031

missions.profile: Aditya-L1, India's first dedicated solar observatory, studies the Sun's corona, chromosphere and solar wind from a halo orbit around the Sun–Earth L1 point.
Near-Earth Object Surveyor, a NASA infrared space telescope designed to find and characterise potentially hazardous asteroids and comets that approach Earth.
ESA's planetary defence mission to the binary asteroid system Didymos–Dimorphos, which will survey the aftermath of NASA's DART impact on Dimorphos.
missions.status: In transit; first separate views of Didymos and Dimorphos

missions.profile: Technology-demonstration CubeSats supported by ESA and developed with the National and Kapodistrian University of Athens, testing optical communications on small satellites.
missions.status: ERMIS-3 laser link to ground achieved

items.title: NASA's twin ESCAPADE spacecraft complete powered Earth flybys and head for Mars
items.summary: Both ESCAPADE (Escape and Plasma Acceleration and Dynamics Explorers) spacecraft completed a powered Earth flyby, combining Earth's gravity with a sustained engine burn to slingshot toward Mars. With the maneuvers complete, the twin spacecraft are now en route to the Red Planet.

items.title: Tiangong space station experiment chills atoms to a record 9.7 picokelvin
items.summary: Chinese scientists cooled an atomic quantum gas to 9.7 picokelvin aboard the Tiangong space station, reported as a record-low temperature.

items.title: CHAPEA Mission 2 crew completes 378-day simulated Mars mission
items.summary: Four research volunteers — Ross Elder, Ellen Ellis, James Spicer and Matthew Montgomery — exited NASA's Mars Dune Alpha habitat on Oct. 31 after 378 days, completing the agency's second yearlong Mars surface simulation under the Crew Health and Performance Exploration Analog (CHAPEA). The crew lived without windows, outside sounds or real-time calls with family during the mission.

items.title: Antarctic ozone hole reaches its 2026 maximum
items.summary: The 2026 ozone hole ranked seventh largest by area in 48 years of monitoring, according to NASA's Earth Observatory, but it was not as deep as other large holes on record.

items.title: GSLV-F18/NVS-03 mission
items.summary: India's Press Information Bureau published an official note on ISRO's GSLV-F18 mission, which carried the NVS-03 navigation satellite for the NavIC system.

items.title: Pakistani astronaut to be first foreign astronaut aboard Tiangong
items.summary: An astronaut from Pakistan will be the first foreign astronaut to fly to China's Tiangong space station, according to multiple reports.

items.title: Rubin Observatory spots trans-Neptunian object orbiting opposite to the planets
items.summary: The Vera C. Rubin Observatory has detected an object beyond Neptune whose orbit runs against the direction of the planets.

items.title: Rubin Observatory discovers two new satellite galaxies of the Milky Way
items.summary: The Vera C. Rubin Observatory has found two previously unknown dim satellites of the Milky Way. Reports note that hundreds more such companions may await discovery.

items.title: Hubble image of globular cluster Messier 30
items.summary: A new NASA/ESA Hubble Space Telescope image shows the globular star cluster Messier 30 (M30), also catalogued as NGC 7099.

items.title: Euclid images the Milky Way's galactic bulge
items.summary: For one day, ESA's Euclid space telescope turned from its dark-Universe survey to image the extremely bright inner region of the Milky Way known as the galactic bulge.

items.title: India outlines Swachh Space Mission 2030 to tackle orbital debris
items.summary: India plans a Swachh Space Mission 2030 aimed at cleaning up orbital debris, with reporting outlining ISRO's strategy and key details.

items.title: Euclid discovers its first new comet
items.summary: ESA's Euclid space telescope has discovered its first previously unknown comet, found in images taken between 16 and 24 September 2026.

items.title: City lights of the US Midwest to the East Coast seen from the ISS
items.summary: An image from the International Space Station shows city lights stretching from the midwestern United States to the East Coast a couple of hours before sunrise.

items.title: China performs precision laser-cutting experiment in space
items.summary: China has carried out what is reported as the world's first precision laser-cutting experiment in space.

items.title: NASA space telescope re-enters Earth's atmosphere after mission 11 times longer than planned
items.summary: A NASA space telescope fell back to Earth after a mission that lasted 11 times longer than originally planned, PBS reports.

items.title: Parker Solar Probe reports an unexpected finding in the solar wind
items.summary: SciTechDaily reports a new, unexpected discovery from NASA's Parker Solar Probe in the turbulent environment of space near the Sun.

items.title: NOIRLab image: the landscape surrounding Rubin Observatory
items.summary: NOIRLab released an image titled "Earthly Expanse Around Rubin" showing the terrain surrounding the Vera C. Rubin Observatory in Chile.

items.title: Hubble study finds dwarf galaxies keep little of the oxygen their stars make
items.summary: A Hubble Space Telescope image of dwarf galaxy NGC 4449 accompanies results from the Galaxies Losing Oxygen via Winds (GLOW) study. Researchers found that dwarf galaxies retain only a small fraction of the oxygen produced by their stars.

items.title: Rubin Observatory spots dwarf planet candidate beyond Pluto
items.summary: The Vera C. Rubin Observatory has identified a possible new dwarf planet orbiting beyond Pluto.

items.title: CSA astronaut Joshua Kutryk installs new roll-out solar array during ISS spacewalk
items.summary: Expedition 75 flight engineer Joshua Kutryk of the Canadian Space Agency was photographed during a spacewalk to install a new roll-out solar array on the port side truss of the International Space Station.

items.title: Chang'e-6 far-side samples reveal chemical clue to the Moon-forming impact
items.summary: Analysis of Moon rocks returned by China's Chang'e-6 mission has revealed a chemical clue to the giant impact thought to have formed the Moon.
